//: TypeScript is opt-in per file. The framework layer stays JavaScript, and a team can write new
specs, commands, or configs in .ts without converting anything — allowJs keeps both in one
strict is on deliberately: a suite that permits `any` gives up the checking TypeScript was
adopted for, and the framework rules already forbid the shortcuts that make strict painful.
checkJs stays off so adopting TypeScript does not begin with hundreds of pre-existing errors
in .js code nobody is changing. Turn it on per-file with // @ts-check when you are ready.
Comments cannot live inside compilerOptions — tsc rejects unknown options there.
